newsitem.title: USA: Marcus says Star Wars boosts Q4 movie revs.
newsitem.headline: Marcus says Star Wars boosts Q4 movie revs.

text.p: Marcus Corp chairman Stephen Marcus said sold-out shows for the "Star Wars" trilogy has boosted revenues for the fourth quarter ending May 30 at the company's movie business.
"We had three blockbusters back-to-back where we were selling all the seats," Marcus told Reuters in an interview.
The successful theatre season means revenue from the movie business will account for about 30 percent of Marcus' total revenues for the fourth quarter, up from about 25 percent.
He did not further detail the gains and would not comment on analysts' profit estimates as a matter of policy.

Marcus Corp, founded by Steve Marcus' father Ben, is also buying up movie theatres faster than its original gameplan. Marcus said the company had planned to have 400 screens by the end of the year 2000, but will have that many two years ahead of schedule by the end of 1998. By the end of the year 2000 the company plans to have between 500 and 600 screens.

In the hotel and resort business, Marcus said he expects better profit margins ahead for two reasons. Some significant pre-opening costs are now fully accounted for and will not be included in future statements and he sees general strength in the high-end sector of the hotel industry.

The hotel and resort business accounts for about 20 percent of the company's total revenues but has margins of only about eight percent. By 1997, the profit margin in the business should be 10 percent and move to 13 percent in 1998, he said.
In the company's motel business, which accounts for about 45 percent of its revenues, Marcus said "it firmed up nicely."
Marcus Corp owns Budgetel Inns and just spent $2.5 million adding amenities aimed at business travelers to 10 percent of the rooms at each Budgetel.
He said "we're not seeing the RevPar increases of a few years ago but it is up a little" in the motel segment. RevPar is revenue per available room.
He said he was puzzled by the company's current stock price, which has been in a range of about $20-$24 since July.
"We did a study where we just valued the pieces, if we sold off our assets ... and our base value, the floor, should be about $30," Marcus said, noting that the company owns all its own real estate.
He said capital expenditures should total about $100 million at year-end compared with $83.7 million in fiscal 1996.
